description: Django 5.1 + Django REST Framework vocabulary, drafted under the held-out protocol from the official docs only (no testbed read). Adds to _base; never removes. Covers the ORM's single-object reads and shortcuts, the request.user ownership idioms and DRF object-permission hooks, request.POST / request.data as mass-assignment sources with ModelForm / serializer validation as the allow-list, F() for check-then-write, min_value as the numeric bound, and the ORM's write methods. P7 (2026-09-15, after the held-out run): four class-scope/route slots added from the DRF permissions, generic-views and routers docs; no existing value changed. 2026-10 (schema v3, after the held-out run, held-out NOT re-run): request_sources from the request-response and DRF requests docs; no existing value changed.

authz_guard.note: Docs ownership idiom: `obj.owner == request.user` (DRF IsOwnerOrReadOnly) or a lookup scoped with `owner=request.user`; both operand orders and .id/.pk forms listed. `request.user` alone proves only login (authn_only). Model-level checks (permission_required, has_perm, is_staff) count as authorization, like the reference pack's role checks.

authn_only.note: permission_classes / check_permissions prove only that DRF's view-level list ran (typically IsAuthenticated); an object-level class in it is matched by authz_guard. user_passes_test tests the user, not the object.

lock_guard.note: F(): docs 'Avoiding race conditions using F()' - the database applies the write. Matched only where an F(...) call can sit (`stock=F(`, `= F(`, `(F(`, `models.F(`) so calls whose name merely ends in f are not matched. atomic / select_for_update / transaction come from _base.

allowlist_guard.note: A ModelForm or serializer declares its writable fields (docs: 'explicitly set all fields'), so writing via is_valid()/cleaned_data/validated_data is an allow-list by construction. save(update_fields=[...]) is an explicit list on the write.

positive_guard.note: min_value= on IntegerField/DecimalField maps to MinValueValidator; Positive*Field enforces >= 0. `<= 0` / `< 0` are the negated forms of a clean_<field>() check (`if value < 0: raise ValidationError`).

mass_assign_signal.note: request.GET is absent: lower-cased it is a prefix of request.get_host / get_full_path / get_signed_cookie. QueryDict.dict() is the docs' way to turn POST into a plain mapping.

qty_terms.note: num_ is the docs' counter prefix (num_employees, num_chairs, num_books); votes is the tutorial's counter.

price_terms.note: General money words; the docs only use price, which _base has.

orm_read_calls.note: Not `get`: dict.get / request.POST.get would make every method with an id parameter a candidate; async aget has no such collision. get_object is DRF's detail read; object permissions apply only if check_object_permissions runs, which authz_guard matches.

dyn_write_calls.note: QuerySet.update(**mapping), update_or_create(defaults=mapping). `create` left out: the docs' create() takes explicit kwargs and would fire on every ordinary insert.

commit_calls.note: Django autocommits, so the ORM write itself is the commit. perform_* are DRF's save/deletion hooks.

id_param_exact.note: DetailView pk_url_kwarg / slug_url_kwarg defaults, DRF lookup_field='pk', the <uuid:> converter.

scoped_read_calls.note: P7. DRF/CBV get_object() filters through get_queryset() and runs check_object_permissions(); the class is the guard's home.

object_permission_hooks.note: P7. A project permission class defining has_object_permission() is object-level (DRF permissions guide).

route_markers.note: P7. urls.py path()/re_path() name the view; router.register() and .as_view() name the class, so every method of it is reachable.

request_sources.note: 2026-10. HttpRequest.GET/POST/FILES/COOKIES/META/body/headers (ref/request-response) and DRF Request.data/query_params (api-guide/requests), lower-cased: origin text is matched lower-cased. request.get also covers request.GET.get(...).
